assessment: CSV delivery remains required. Two alternative interface changes could remove coordinator reconciliation or replacement-request dependencies. The observations support investigating these dependencies, not either causal explanation. Feasibility within six engineer-days and the hosting allowance remains unverified.

openings.claim: Hypothesis: bind an export to a center-authorized course-week manifest using stable internal course identities, rather than deriving its scope from current instructor assignments or course names. A shared scope contract could make Monday comparison with a separate schedule unnecessary.
openings.delta: Replace inference from mutable labels and assignments with an explicit scope handoff. Former comparison obligations remain: establish the intended courses and week, resolve renames and splits, detect omissions, and identify who may correct scope. The manifest must also count courses with no attendance rows.
openings.prediction: If mutable identity drives the omissions, fixing scope while varying instructor assignments and names will preserve the intended course set; an incomplete manifest will still fail.
openings.probe: In fabricated staging cases, compare incumbent and manifest exports for assignment changes, renames, and a split. Six coordinators specify intended scope before seeing results. Count omissions, foreign-center rows, and total manifest upkeep plus handling time. Check unchanged CSV imports, concurrent attendance entry, engineering effort, and hosting cost before adoption.
assumptions: Stable identities and week-specific scope can be represented within budget.
Coordinators can establish scope without shifting excessive work upstream.

openings.claim: Hypothesis: expose the existing exporter through an authenticated center/week request interface with a retrievable completion result, so coordinators can obtain replacements without an intermediary request-and-wait cycle.
openings.delta: Remove dependence on operator availability. Preserve its obligations: authorize center scope, validate the requested week and courses, signal failures, and identify the latest completed file. Keep the documented CSV and private delivery; export reads must allow attendance entry.
openings.prediction: Replacement elapsed time should approach execution plus retrieval time. Active handling and course-set accuracy may remain unchanged, which would limit this alternative's contribution to the success measure.
openings.probe: Time a fabricated replacement through both interfaces, separating active handling from waiting. Test forged center requests, simultaneous attendance entry, and bounded repeat requests. Reject the change if authorization, schema, six-day effort, or hosting checks fail; retain the next-40-export outcome test.
assumptions: Existing execution can be safely exposed within budget.
Replacement delay substantially reflects mediation rather than necessary scope correction.
